title: VQ logical expert codebook
hypothesis: A shared physical expert decoder plus quantized Mirror coordinates can represent many logical expert functions with materially fewer serialized bytes than independent experts while preserving held-out function quality.
physical_object: one shared 32D linear expert base plus a shared 4D functional basis and codebook decoder
mirror_coordinate: one learned VQ index per logical expert selecting a residual function coordinate
logical_multiplicity: 64 expert functions selected by router IDs
controls: shared low-rank functional basis with FP32 coordinates
full-vector learned VQ codebook plus expert indices
shared-basis Mirror coordinates plus VQ codebook and indices

task.teacher: shared Gaussian base plus four shared orthogonal residual directions with correlated Gaussian coordinates; train/dev and fresh banks independently sampled

development.allowed: fit codebooks and choose K on development only; fixed Lloyd algorithm and predeclared K sweep

paid_objects: per-expert full vectors for independent control

success_gate: At some K, every fresh world has NRMSE <=0.05, payload <=50% of independent experts, and no more than 2% duplicate codes; compare low-rank and generic VQ controls at matched quality.
failure_gate: No fresh K meets quality and byte gates, code collisions exceed gate, or generic shared-basis/VQ control matches Mirror without a Mirror-specific benefit.
boundaries: Synthetic linear functions with shared low-dimensional residual structure only.
This does not establish neural MoE training, routing quality, or general capacity.
Logical expert count is not capacity; held-out function quality and collisions determine utility.
